title: Quantum Hamiltonian time crystals from covariant quantum Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert relaxation
abstract: Classical Hamiltonian time crystals are constrained energy minima that move along symmetry orbits at frequencies set by Lagrange multipliers. We construct quantum counterparts by minimizing the energy over density matrices with fixed spectrum and charge expectations. A symmetry-covariant quantum Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation selects them as periodic attractors, preserving the spectrum and fixing the multipliers dynamically. A chiral spin trimer motivated by Cu$_3$ molecular magnets realizes this motion at a prepared magnetization, without a Zeeman term.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to construct quantum Hamiltonian time crystals using a symmetry-covariant quantum Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (qLLG) equation. By analyzing the energy minimization and subsequent dynamics, the authors demonstrate that the system settles into a stable, periodic motion along a symmetry orbit when constrained by non-zero magnetization. This offers a constructive pathway to observe time-periodic quantum states in magnetic molecular magnets.
main_problem: The paper constructs and analyzes quantum Hamiltonian time crystals, which are periodic attractors in the density matrix evolution, circumventing theoretical constraints for closed Hamiltonian systems.
main_result: The covariant quantum Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (qLLG) dynamics provide a constructive method to realize these time crystals, showing periodic motion along symmetry orbits for specific charge constraints.
method: The analysis involves minimizing the energy expectation value subject to fixed spectrum and charge expectations, and then simulating the evolution using the symmetry-covariant qLLG equation.
model_or_system: The model is a chiral spin trimer system, motivated by Cu3 molecular magnets, governed by an SU(2)-invariant Hamiltonian. The dynamics are described by a generalized qLLG equation acting on the density matrix.
key_observables: Time crystal frequency, magnetization ($\langle\mathbf{J}angle$), terminal covariant velocity ($\|D_tho\|$), and coherence amplitudes.
important_parameters: Damping parameter ($\kappa$), charge expectation ($q$), and the ratio of energy gap to exchange gap ($ eta\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of a unique solution for the Lagrange multipliers and relies on the qLLG flow to drive the system towards the periodic attractor.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy landscape $E_{\min}(q)$ versus charge $q$, and show time evolution of observables like magnetization and coherences, confirming periodicity for the time crystal regime.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by defining the time crystal condition via energy minimization. It then introduces and analyzes the dynamics using the qLLG equation, detailing the behavior in different coherence regimes (e.g., doublet-mixing branch) and confirming the approach to equilibrium or periodic motion.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, dynamical mechanism (the qLLG equation) to stabilize and observe non-equilibrium quantum states (time crystals) in condensed matter systems, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and non-equilibrium dynamics.
